section_1_complete_textbook_notes.chapter_overview: This chapter investigates line (reflectional) symmetry and rotational symmetry. It covers lines of symmetry, mirror halves, center of rotation, order of rotational symmetry, smallest angle of symmetry, and symmetry properties of regular polygons and cultural artifacts like the Ashoka Chakra.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A figure possesses line symmetry if a line divides it into two mirror halves that overlap perfectly when folded.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: An axis dividing a shape into two mirror-image halves that coincide under reflection/folding.
mathematical_definitions.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.

formulas_and_properties.name: Regular Polygon Line Symmetry Rule
formulas_and_properties.statement_or_expression: Number of Lines of Symmetry of Regular n-gon = n
formulas_and_properties.direct_example: Equilateral triangle (n=3) has 3 lines of symmetry.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A figure has rotational symmetry if it matches its original appearance after rotation by an angle < 360° around a fixed center point.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: Property where a shape maps onto itself when rotated by an angle less than 360° around its center.

formulas_and_properties.name: Smallest Angle of Rotational Symmetry
formulas_and_properties.statement_or_expression: Smallest Angle = 360° / Order of Rotational Symmetry
formulas_and_properties.variable_definitions: Order = number of matching orientations in 360°

section_2_step_by_step_algorithms.method_name: Determining Rotational Symmetry Order and Angle
step_by_step_instructions: Step 1: Fix center point of rotation.
Step 2: Rotate shape 360° and count how many times it looks identical to original position (Order n).

model_textbook_example.problem: Find the smallest rotational angle for Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes).

section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.question_text: Can a shape have rotational symmetry with a smallest angle of 17°?
section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.complete_solution: No, because 360° is not an exact integer multiple of 17° (360 / 17 = 21.176...).

section_4_complete_textbook_exercise_sol.question_text: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
